beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent.
beats.got: There are four things I can share instead of 'the agent', and picking one is a strategy call. That is my team's problem exactly.

beats.trigger: A licence rollout, a portal, or a shared drive works.
beats.got: I should bring a story of a tool people got and didn't use. I have one, the BI portal.

beats.trigger: **Test** the switch assumptions and name one person and one test to take out of the room
beats.got: Four verbs. The last one, one person and one test, is what I care about.

beats.trigger: What would you want a teammate to have: your `memory/` folder, one of your skills, the morning output, or a way to ask the agent a question in Slack? And why that one?
beats.got: A concrete choice. It is my fourteen-person problem put as a question.

beats.trigger: Start with the teammate's work, not with *"what should I share with my teammate?"*
beats.got: Start from the job my teammate has to do, not from what I built. Jobs-to-be-Done is familiar from consulting.

beats.trigger: If it could describe anyone in the room, point to the generic line and ask the agent to try that part again.
beats.got: A check I can apply: does jtbd.md name one person and an outcome I could observe? If not, send it back.

beats.trigger: If the reason is *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: Choosing by what the infrastructure allows is the mistake. That is how we picked the BI portal.

beats.trigger: finds what would stop that candidate from being absorbed and turns it into a technical plan plus a people plan.
beats.got: Nothing new. This is a signpost to the next exercise.

beats.trigger: Find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can absorb it, then draft both halves of the plan.
beats.got: Find the one obstacle that decides it, then write two plans.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: Don't list the obstacles. Find the one that keeps the others hard. Useful, and I can test it.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: My plans usually have names missing on the people side. This tells me to treat that as the result, not a gap to fill later.

beats.trigger: checks the assumptions underneath these plans, imagines the failure, and writes the first real-world contact
beats.got: Nothing new. Next exercise tests the plans.

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: My plans are guesses until a teammate touches them.

beats.trigger: *what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?*
beats.got: A sharper question than 'how do I get adoption'. It gives a short list of conditions I can check this week.

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
beats.got: A pre-mortem that ends in one person, one question and one test for Monday. That is the output I wanted.

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping.
beats.got: A recap of the whole sequence. The shopping versus design line is the part I'll keep.

beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Access is a switch somebody flips, and it completes in a minute.
beats.got: Rollout numbers measure access, not use. I already knew that, but it is stated cleanly.

beats.trigger: The leadership had not done the analysis. People they trusted had.
beats.got: A real story where the analysis was good and the decision never came, because leaders trust people, not analyses. My CFO behaves the same way.

beats.trigger: Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
beats.got: Context, boundary and checks copy easily. Someone answering for the agent does not. I need to name that person for my team.

beats.trigger: Pick the one your teammate's week can take in.
beats.got: Nothing new. This repeats the four strategies from earlier, now with what each asks of the receiver.

beats.trigger: Not *how do I get them to adopt this?* but *what would have to be true for them to switch?*
beats.got: Nothing new. I did this question in the exercise already.

beats.trigger: Have the conversation before you build anything more.
beats.got: Talk to one person before building anything else. Their answer tells me which plan to keep.

beats.trigger: Who gets your context, who gets a skill, who wants only the output, and who would use an @mention?
beats.got: Sort my fourteen people across the four strategies. Probably not one answer for everyone.

beats.trigger: - Write the technical plan and the people plan together.
beats.got: nothing new, a summary of what I just did

beats.trigger: Their answer is the evidence. The plan is still the hypothesis.
beats.got: Come back with what the person said. It counts as evidence and the plan does not.

beats.trigger: ## Next
beats.got: nothing new

take_homes: Choose what to share by the teammate's job and the outcome I can observe, not by what our platform allows. Context, skill, pushed output and pull interface are the four options. Sharing 'the agent' isn't one of them.
Write the technical plan and the people plan together. Unnamed owners in the people plan are the finding.
One person, one conversation about how they do the job today, before I build anything more.

monday.move: Talk to one person on my team who will receive the pilot-cohort brief. Ask how they do that job today and what would have to be true for them to use the brief. Write the answer into monday.md.
monday.who: One of my fourteen. I would pick the one who owns the usage-pricing numbers and is most likely to say no.
monday.when: Monday, thirty minutes, before I touch the brief again.
monday.stop_condition: If their current way of doing it already works for them and they can't name what would make them switch, I stop building the brief for them and look at someone else.
monday.blocker: We have no shared place for the context files. Everyone keeps their own copy, so even if the person says yes, I can't hand over the context.

misconception.why: I still think good prompts matter. But the module's point is that sharing fails on absorption, not on how good the agent is. My team's problem is the missing shared place and the missing owner, and no prompt fixes either. It is not fully changed, because I did not see a prompt-quality case here either way.

one_line: Useful if you have a team to bring along. The first two exercises gave me something to run on Monday, and the lecture mostly repeated them.
